newsitem.title: USA: Burlington sees rest of year hurt by denim.
newsitem.headline: Burlington sees rest of year hurt by denim.

text.p: Burlington Industries Inc said Monday it sees an inventory correction in its denim business cutting earnings by $0.10-$0.15 per share for the rest of the fiscal year.

"We are encouraged that our results were equal to last year's second quarter, despite the weakness in denim, which is the result of inventory reductions in the supply chain," said George Henderson, president and chief executive officer.

"Although the tone of the denim business is better, we expect that the denim inventory correction will continue into the September quarter and as a result, will negatively impact earnings for the remaining half of the fiscal year by $0.10 to $0.15 per share," he said.

Burlington Industries said Monday earnings per share for the second quarter of fiscal year 1997 were $0.34 per share including a net gain of $0.01 per share from non-recurring items, compared with $0.33 per share for the second quarter of fiscal year 1996.
